entries.root_cause: The ECMAScript braced Unicode escape decoder constrained textual width to six hex digits instead of validating the decoded code-point value. Leading-zero padding could therefore encode an otherwise forbidden ASCII identifier while evading semantic matching.

The non-ASCII fail-closed check ran only on source spelling before language-level Unicode escapes were decoded. An ASCII escape could therefore materialize a cross-script confusable identifier after the confusable fence had already passed.

Forbidden concepts were compared against whole normalized identifiers only. Ordinary snake_case and camelCase compositions such as fetch_metrics or MetricsRepository could contain a forbidden capability as an identifier component without equaling the forbidden token.

Morphological variants were enforced for code identifiers but not for path components. Plural directory names such as metrics, problems or resource-inventories therefore bypassed the forbidden path capability fence.

Shared-Monitoring persistence protection relied on a contiguous literal SQL spelling. Quoted schema identifiers, comments and equivalent DDL formatting could therefore create G2-owned persistence while bypassing the structural marker.

A finite capability vocabulary was still being treated as sufficient proof of bounded G2 behavior. Equivalent excluded behavior could be expressed through generic persistence, provider-native authorization or secret data-flow primitives without using any enumerated forbidden name.

JavaScript regex-literal eligibility in comment masking and assignment scanning was inferred only from punctuation, so a regex beginning after an expression-leading keyword such as typeof could be misread as division and a double slash inside its character class could then be masked as a line comment, erasing downstream secret provenance.
horizontal_audit: regex literals after void return and yield

entries.root_cause: Secret-sink invocation equivalence covered optional direct calls and ordinary call/apply helper invocation but omitted optional invocation of the call/apply helper itself, allowing the same governed sink to receive raw credentials through call?.(...) or apply?.(...).

Static computed sink recognition accepted bracket access only when the bracket followed the receiver directly, so JavaScript optional computed member access with the semantically equivalent receiver?.[member] form escaped sink classification even when followed by an optional call.

SQL-bearing tagged-template extraction accepted bare and dotted tag expressions but not statically computed or balanced-grouped member tags, allowing authority-changing SQL passed to a governed execution call to evade SQL-surface classification.
horizontal_audit: query execute exec run and sql calls
